children.text: Antipolo Cathedral enshrines the image of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage and is one of the Philippines' best-known pilgrimage sites. In 2024 it became the first international shrine in the Philippines and Southeast Asia. It is close to Manila, so it works as a half-day trip, and paired with the waterfall park and art museum in the same city it makes a full day.

The shrine's official name is the International Shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage. It stands in the hill city of Antipolo, east of Manila, and also serves as the seat of the Diocese of Antipolo. The dark-skinned Madonna enshrined inside has been venerated since the Spanish era, and millions of pilgrims are said to visit each year. True to its name, Filipinos associate it with prayers for peace and safe journeys.

Its history goes back to 1591, when the Jesuits built the first church here. The church was completed around 1632 and received the image. According to tradition, the image was found on a tipolo tree and vanished several times, each time reappearing at the same tree. The church was burned during a rebellion by the Chinese community in 1639 and was damaged by earthquakes in 1645, 1824 and 1863. Records also show that on June 6, 1868, the young José Rizal came here with his father to fulfill a vow his mother had made.

During World War II, Japanese forces used the church as a garrison and arsenal, while the image was hidden in a nearby kitchen and later moved to Angono, Pasig and Quiapo. The building was destroyed by Allied bombardment in 1945, and the image returned to Antipolo on October 15 of that year. The present church is a modern building designed by architect Jose de Ocampo, begun in 1948 and completed in 1954. It has a concrete structure with a dome and clerestory windows, and a carved wooden relief shows the image's first arrival in the Philippines. It became the country's first national shrine on January 14, 1954, and a cathedral when the diocese was established on June 25, 1983.

The Vatican's decision arrived in March 2023, granting international shrine status, and the solemn declaration took place on January 26, 2024. In February of that year the shrine received the Golden Rose sent by the Pope. In 2026 the Diocese of Antipolo marked 400 years of devotion to the image and the 100th anniversary of its canonical coronation with a jubilee year; the cathedral's jubilee door opened on January 14 and the jubilee runs until November 28.Word that it is the first international shrine in the Philippines and Southeast Asia has increased visitor numbers in recent years. For travelers from abroad, it is both a religious site and a place to see Filipino devotional life up close. This guide explains how non-Catholics can visit respectfully, and why you should or should not go during pilgrimage season. Weekday mornings are the calmest, while on Sundays Masses follow one another and the church fills up. The church itself takes about an hour, but adding the snack stalls, museum, nearby waterfall park and art museum turns it into a satisfying half day or full day. Its closeness to central Manila makes it easy to fit into a short stay.

blocks.title: The Black Madonna and the main altar

children.text: The heart of the church is the main altar, where the image of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage is enshrined. One travel guide says the image now inside the church is a replica, so check locally how the original is shown. Avoid taking photos during Mass and look around quietly. Simply walking slowly behind the altar and along the side aisles, and respectfully watching worshippers pray, gives you a feel for Filipino Catholic devotion.

Designed by architect Jose de Ocampo, the building has a dome with clerestory windows, a bishop's chair and a pipe organ. Classified as a modern, Art Deco-related church, it feels very different from a Spanish Baroque church. The wooden relief showing the image's first arrival in the Philippines is also worth a look.

blocks.title: International shrine and the Golden Rose

children.text: The January 2024 declaration made it the first international shrine in the Philippines and Southeast Asia, and in February the Pope's Golden Rose arrived. It is presented as the first Marian church in Asia to receive the Golden Rose. You can see this history on signs and commemorative displays.

blocks.title: Small museum and gift shop behind the church

children.text: Behind the church is a small museum on the history of the image, with a gift shop below it, as far as is known. Rosaries, Marian medals and candles are common souvenirs. Opening hours change often, so check locally. Many people buy a Marian medal or rosary as a keepsake, and at the candle sellers on the street in front you can see worshippers lighting prayer candles.
On Holy Thursday and Good Friday, and again from the evening of
April 30
to the early morning of
May 1
, pilgrims walk from Quiapo Church in Manila to Antipolo. Reports before Holy Thursday 2026 expected close to three million pilgrims. If you only want to sightsee, it is safer to avoid these dates.

In front of the church and along the street, stalls sell snacks such as roasted cashews (kasuy) and kalamay (a sticky rice cake). They are considered Antipolo specialties and Filipinos often buy them as gifts. Prices are usually marked rather than haggled, but check locally. Cashews come salted and roasted or sweetened, so try a small bag of each before choosing. Kalamay is a sticky rice sweet made by simmering coconut milk and sugar, so it goes best with water on hot days.

Antipolo is a hill city, and restaurants along Sumulong Highway are described as offering views over the city while you dine. At sunset, some spots look toward the lights of Manila. It makes a good dinner stop after visiting the church. The road has many sharp curves, so slow down if you are driving.

children.text: Leave Manila and reach central Antipolo by LRT-2 Antipolo Station, taxi or Grab.
Enter the church, pause in front of the main altar and look around the building inside and out. If Mass is under way, watch quietly.
See the museum and gift shop behind the church, then try cashews and kalamay at the plaza stalls.
Have lunch at a town restaurant serving Filipino home cooking.
Take a tricycle or Grab to Hinulugang Taktak park, about
1.7km

During pilgrimage season and on weekends, town roads are heavily congested, so allow double the travel time.
See the image and main altar at the church, then look around the museum.
Take a short walk in Hinulugang Taktak park.
Have lunch in town.
Go to the Pinto Art Museum to see the galleries and gardens, and return to Manila before dark.
Get off at Antipolo, the eastern LRT-2 terminus. Near the side opposite SM City Masinag, transfer to a jeepney marked Antipolo Simbahan. Allow extra time for the road journey to the cathedral.

The church can be visited any time of year, and it is quiet if you avoid Mass times. December to April, when rain is lighter, is the easiest time to travel.

From late April to July, however, pilgrimage season makes it the most crowded. If you want photos or quiet viewing, choose a weekday morning. If you want the cultural experience, go during pilgrimage season but be ready for the crowds.

Antipolo is a day trip from Manila, so most travelers stay in Manila or Quezon City. There are hotels around the church, but they are hard to book in pilgrimage season, so check ahead. Hotel names and rates vary a lot by season, so check recent reviews on booking sites.

The best-known food here is the roasted cashews and kalamay from the plaza stalls. The town has fast-food outlets and Filipino home-cooking restaurants, and restaurants along Sumulong Highway let you dine with a view of the city. For street food, choose stalls where you can see the hygiene for yourself.
Dress modestly, covering shoulders and knees, and avoid taking photos or talking during Mass.
Look around quietly, and do not block worshippers' prayer spots.
Some areas are on hills, so comfortable shoes help.
From late April to July is pilgrimage season, so a weekday morning is better.
Mass and confession times are reported inconsistently, so check the church's official channels before you go.
Keep belongings in a front bag and watch your phone in the crowded plaza.
Combining the church with Hinulugang Taktak or the Pinto Art Museum makes for a fuller day.
Alay Lakad dates vary by year, so check the latest announcements.
On Holy Thursday, Good Friday and April 30–May 1, millions of people converge, and roads can be closed and public transport paralyzed.
In pilgrimage season, parking near the church and booking a taxi are almost impossible, so be prepared to walk.
Pickpocketing and phone snatching are common when crowds are large.
Bring water and a hat for the midday heat from March to May.
Because it is a religious site, shorts and sleeveless tops may not be allowed in.
Opening hours and Mass times can change, so check the latest announcements.
